subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York houses an extensive collection of ancient pottery.
• The museum is renowned for its diverse ceramic artifacts.
• The collection includes both earthenware and porcelain pieces.
• Earthenware is made from clay fired at relatively low temperatures.
• Porcelain is made from clay fired at very high temperatures.
prompt: The student wants to contrast the two types of pottery. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Earthenware is made from clay fired at relatively low temperatures, whereas porcelain is made from clay fired at very high temperatures.
choices.B: Both earthenware and porcelain pieces can be found in the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York.
choices.C: Featuring both earthenware and porcelain pieces, the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York is renowned for its diverse ceramic artifacts.
choices.D: Among the diverse ceramic artifacts at the Metropolitan Museum of Art are earthenware pieces, made from clay fired at relatively low temperatures.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer. The sentence contrasts the two types of pottery, noting that earthenware is made from clay fired at relatively low temperatures, whereas porcelain is made from clay fired at very high temperatures.
